focus.jnote: The scan found nothing to take — that is the story, and the tape explains why. Over the weekend U.S. forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz, and Tehran responded with attacks on the UAE and Jordan, marking a resumption of hostilities after roughly a month of relative calm. Oil is elevated — Brent climbed above the $90 mark to $90.31 a barrel while WTI rose to $85.41, and Trump extended military threats to Kharg Island, Iran’s key oil export hub. On rates: the 10-year Treasury yield climbed to around 4.78% on Tuesday, its highest level since January 2025 as rising oil prices and hawkish Fed signals strengthened rate-hike expectations, with markets now pricing in a more than 65% chance of a September hike, up from around 36% before Warsh’s remarks. This is exactly the open-ended headline tape a Sniper does not sell premium into — and the scanner agreed by boarding zero.
focus.notdown: No bullish single-name boarded. Energy and defense are the natural war-premium bids — oil supply fear lifts energy, conflict-demand lifts the defense primes — but these are two-sided war trades, not clean Snipers. One credible de-escalation or ceasefire headline and crude gives back the spike, gapping any bull put the wrong way. Watch-only, nothing to underwrite today.
focus.notup: No bearish single-name boarded. Airlines and other fuel-sensitive cyclicals are pressured by the oil spike, and long-duration tech is squeezed by the 10-year at ~4.79% — but selling bear calls into a VIX that is starting to lift, with a peace-headline squeeze risk on any de-escalation, is its own blow-up. The disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Three reasons. First, the scan boarded zero names — there is simply nothing that passed the gates. Second, the environment: an active U.S.–Iran military exchange in the Strait of Hormuz with Brent above $90 is an unscheduled, open-ended tail you cannot time or size around. Third, macro: a hawkish Warsh has lifted Sept-hike odds to ~57–65% and the 10-year is at ~4.79%, the highest since January 2025, with August jobs Friday stacked on top. P(≥1% gap) at 44% is well above the 35% trigger and composite 66 is deep in WARM. Stand down on new credit spreads, keep cash, re-run tomorrow pre-open.

risks: Iran retaliation & escalation — Tehran responded to the Larak Island strikes with attacks on the UAE and Jordan, resuming hostilities after roughly a month of calm; any further strike on personnel or bases gaps the whole tape instantly. This is the number-one thing to watch.

Strait of Hormuz shipping — a supertanker caught fire after hitting two naval mines in the southern Strait of Hormuz, per Iranian state media, and Trump extended military threats to Kharg Island, Iran’s key oil export hub. Any attack on that infrastructure or a closure sends crude (and jet fuel) vertical — the week’s biggest tail.

Oil → inflation → the 10-year — oil advanced for a second straight day after the Hormuz strike, and higher energy costs are fueling inflation concerns and strengthening expectations for tighter Fed policy. The 10Y at ~4.79% is the highest since Jan 2025 and a further rate pop compounds pressure on stocks.

Hawkish Warsh & the Sept FOMC — markets are now pricing in a more than 65% chance of a September hike, up from around 36% before Warsh’s remarks. A hawkish repricing on top of an oil shock is the worst macro combination.

August jobs report · Fri 9/4 — investors are bracing for a busy calendar, with manufacturing/services data due and the highly anticipated August jobs report on Friday. A hot or cold print reprices hike odds again — keep any spread clear of the release; verdict cannot be GREEN into an NFP with VIX expanding.
